    Want a great price on fast nbn®?

    Get up to $26/mth off for 6 months on selected plans.
    For new services, ends 10 August. For FTTP and HFC only. T&Cs apply.

    Up to $26/mth off nbn® deal for 6 months - terms and conditions

    Offer for new services taking up Ultimate and Ultrafast nbn plans until 10 August 2026. For FTTP and HFC only. Monthly discount may end earlier if you change plans.

    For Internet plans with modem included for use: if you cancel, change tech type or to an Internet Only plan, within 24 months, simply return your modem or pay a $200 non-return fee.

    Up to $26/mth off Opticomm deal for 6 months - terms and conditions

    Offer for new services taking up Ultimate and Ultrafast Opticomm plans until 10 August 2026. For FTTP and HFC only.  Monthly discount may end earlier if you change plans.

    For Internet plans with modem included for use: if you cancel, change tech type or to an Internet Only plan, within 24 months, simply return your modem or pay a $200 non-return fee.

    How to get the free upgrade

    1. Choose an eligible higher-speed plan
    2. Fill out the fibre upgrade request form
    3. Place your order.

    We'll handle everything and keep you connected while your upgrade is completed. This takes around 2-4 weeks. Then we'll switch you over and you'll be ready to go - fast! 

    Free upgrade for standard installation only.

    Request your fibre upgrade

    What type of nbn customer are you?

    Let’s get your free nbn fibre upgrade sorted.

    1. Fill out the fibre upgrade request form.
    2. We’ll connect you on a plan that is supported by your current tech type to keep you online during the upgrade.
    3. We’ll reach out to you and start the upgrade.  Allow 2-4 weeks. Then we’ll switch you over to your chosen high-speed plan.

    Eligible plan required. Free upgrade for standard installation only. Additional charges may apply if you require equipment to be installed in a specific location.

    Request upgrade

    Use the My Telstra app to request your tech upgrade.

    1. Open My Telstra on your smart phone.
    2. Tap 'Internet and phone' and then 'View or manage your plan'.
    3. Next tap 'Change your plan' and choose an eligible high-speed plan.
    4. Follow the prompts to complete the fibre upgrade request.

    If you're on des﻿ktop

    Use your smart phone to scan the QR code. If you have My Telstra you'll go directly to Step 3 once signed-in. If you don't have the app, you'll be prompted to download it.

    Still have questions?

    Get the answers you need from our dedicated fibre upgrade team.

    New Development Charge

    What is the New Development Charge?

    The New Development Charge is a $[charge] one-time fee charged by nbn®.

    It applies to dwellings nbn has classified as being without an existing nbn installation. These can include new lots, subdivisions, and granny flats with a separate address from the primary residence.

    Extra charges may apply for non-standard or professional installation of Telstra or nbn co equipment and for premises in new developments.

    Still have questions?

    Message us or call 13 22 00.

    New Connection Charge

    What is the New Connection Charge?

    The New Connection Charge is a $[ocnmCharge] or $[ocwmCharge] one-time fee charged by Opticomm. The fee is for the installation and connection of equipment in new dwellings. The charge amount depends on factors such as additional connections or equipment replacement.

    What is Opticomm?

    Opticomm is the network service provider responsible for installing the internet connection at this address.

    Still have questions?

    Message us or call 13 22 00.

    New Development Charge

    What is the New Development Charge?

    The New Development Charge is a $[charge] one-time fee charged by Opticomm.

    It applies to dwellings Opticomm has classified as being without an existing internet installation. These can include new lots, subdivisions, and granny flats with a separate address from the primary residence.

    Extra charges may apply for non-standard or professional installation of Telstra or Opticomm supplied equipment and for premises in new developments.

    What is Opticomm?

    Opticomm is the network service provider responsible for installing the internet connection at this address.

    Modem compatibility

    Your modem must be nbn-compatible and support the specific nbn technology at your address. So, here’s some things you can check:

    Network compatibility

    Check your modem for an ‘nbn ready’ sticker or contact the manufacturer to confirm it works with our network.

    Tech-type compatibility

    Different nbn technologies need different modem features, like VDSL2 for FTTN and FTTB or Ethernet WAN for FTTP and HFC. For our high speed plans you may need a Cat5e or higher ethernet cable to help achieve the higher speeds.

    Speed compatibility

    Lots of things may contribute to a modem’s achievable Wi-Fi and Ethernet speed, including its age. A modem that is Wi-Fi generation 6 or above is more likely to support higher speeds, especially on faster plans. Check the specs or ask your modem’s manufacturer.

    You may also need to manually configure PPPoE login details, VLAN tagging, and SSID and Wi-Fi settings.

    For help with setup and troubleshooting, refer to our Set up my BYO modem guide.

    If you bring your own modem, troubleshooting support may also be limited and not all My Telstra app features are enabled.

    Frequently asked questions - 5G plans

    It’s home Internet that’s delivered over Telstra’s 5G mobile network. There are no technician visits or network cables needed. You just plug in the modem, it connects to nearby 5G mobile towers, and you’re online.

    Why customers choose 5G Home Internet:

    • Simple, plug‑and‑play setup
    • Fast access without installation delays
    • Flexible month-to-month plans

    Explore Telstra 5G Home Internet plans

    No. You can set up 5G Home Internet up yourself in minutes. 

    1. Place your Telstra 5G modem close to a window and plug it into power.
      TIP: Use our 5G modem optimal placement guide to find your home’s ‘green zone’, where the 5G signal is strongest.
    2. Your 5G modem connects to nearby 5G mobile towers and you’re online. 
    3. Start streaming!

    These pro tips will help you get the best possible speed and performance from your 5G internet signal:

    1. Find your 'green zone'

    • The ‘green zone’ is where the 5G signal is strongest in your home. You can find it using the live tool in our 5G modem optimal placement guide in the My Telstra app.
    • Place your modem by a window in your green zone.

    2. Avoid obstructions

    • Try to avoid windows with buildings, trees or other structures outside that may block 5G signal.
    • Place your modem at least 3 metres away from large metal objects like fridges, microwaves and steel-mesh window security screens to avoid electronic interference.

    3. Choose a raised surface

    • Position your modem on a shelf, table or other surface off the floor, and avoid placing it behind doors such as in a cupboard.
    • If your building has multiple storeys, find a location on the highest level.

    To find these tips in our 5G modem optimal placement guide:

    • Sign in to your my Telstra app
    • Choose your 5G service
    • Go to ‘Improve your connection’
    • Then ‘Tips to improve your 5G signal’.

    The quickest way to find out is to check your address now.

    • Availability depends on 5G internet network capacity in your area, not just whether you have 5G mobile coverage.
    • To help ensure that everyone gets a good experience, we only connect a limited number of customers per area.
    • If 5G Home Internet isn’t available now, it’s worth checking again regularly, because capacity can change.

    Telstra 5G Internet may not be in your area yet, or there may not be enough network capacity to offer the best possible 5G internet experience. This is because:

    • 5G Home internet uses more 5G network capacity than a 5G mobile phone. 
    • We only connect a limited number of homes to 5G Home Internet in each area, to help ensure everyone gets a good experience.
    • This means an area can reach capacity for 5G Home Internet even if 5G mobile coverage is available on your phone.

     Yes. It can be a good idea to keep your nbn service running while you give 5G internet a go. This way you decide which service is right for you. Then once you’ve made your choice, simply cancel the service you don’t want.

    • Will getting 5G Internet automatically cancel my nbn? No. Your nbn service isn’t affected by the 5G service. You’ll need to cancel the nbn service yourself if you decide to switch to 5G Internet.
    • Will I be charged for nbn and 5G at the same time? Yes. You'll still be charged monthly fees for both services while they are active. So you'll pay for two services until you choose which one to cancel.
    • What happens if I cancel the 5G? If you do decide to cancel your 5G Internet within 24 months, simply return your modem in good working order or pay a $200 non-return fee. We’ll provide a free return parcel.

    We don’t recommend 5G Home internet for serious online gamers. Why not?

    • 5G Home Internet can have higher latency than wired connections.
    • Speeds can vary, especially during busy periods.
    • If you need a stable, low‑latency connection for gaming, 5G Home Internet may not be the right choice.

    No, because your Telstra Smart Modem only works at the home address where it’s first set up. If you’re moving:

    • Get in touch with us 
    • We’ll help you cancel your existing 5G Home Internet plan 
    • We’ll try to set you up with a new plan at your new address

    Modem included for use with new 5G Home Internet services. If you cancel or change to a different tech type within 24 months, simply return your modem or pay a $200 non-return fee.

    Yes - as long as the 5G network has enough free capacity at the time. What does this mean?

    • Higher speed 5G plans take up more network capacity or ‘space’ than lower speed 5G plans. 
    • So while it's easy to change down to a lower speed 5G internet plan, you may not be able to change back up to a higher speed 5G internet plan later if there isn't enough capacity on the network in your area at that time. 

    This information is to help you to make the right 5G choice for your needs, not to discourage you from choosing a lower speed plan.

    No, 5G Home Internet doesn’t come with a home phone line. It’s internet only. You should explore nbn plans with Telstra if:

    Why can’t I get this plan?

    Your nbn connection doesn’t support the maximum speeds on this plan.

    The maximum speeds available at your address are dependent on the technology used to connect your premises to the nbn network.

    They will be the same no matter who you buy an internet plan from.

    We don’t offer you this plan so that you don’t pay for speeds your nbn connection can’t achieve.

    This may be due to one of 2 reasons:

    1. The technology at your address is unable to support the speeds included in this plan – so you’d be paying for speeds that you can’t achieve. We only offer you plans based on the maximum upload and download speeds allowable.
    2. At some addresses, we’re unable to estimate the maximum speeds available until you’re on your new plan (particularly if you’re a new customer). Before then, we can’t be sure that the nbn connection at your address can achieve this plan’s speeds. We do this to ensure you don’t pay for speeds you can’t achieve.

    Once you’re connected, if we determine that your technology can support this plan’s speeds, we’ll let you know.

    Your maximum speeds

    The speeds you experience may be lower than the estimated maximum speed ranges for your address, particularly during busy periods, and can be impacted by things like your own setup and wiring. We’ll use the latest information when you’re on your new plan to confirm the maximum speeds at your address. 

    When choosing a plan, you’ll see how the maximum speeds at your address relate to your plan options. This is important because you will not be able to experience the typical or maximum speeds of a plan if the speed available at your address are lower. 

    Additional nbn services

    The maximum available speeds at your address shown are for your existing line only. If you need an additional line/service, we’ll let you know the maximum speeds of the additional line once it’s connected.

    Do I need an additional service?

    Most customers only need one service at their address. Having an additional nbn service at your address means you’ll have to pay for an additional nbn plan and install a new modem.

    If there are no additional available nbn lines at your address, we may need to install a new one, which may increase the time to complete your order, and there may be set-up costs.

    Each nbn line at your address could have different maximum speeds. We’ll ask at checkout about additional nbn services.

    Basic 5G Internet speed

    Great for 1-3 people with light to moderate data use.

    • Staying connected on social media, browsing 
    • Sending and receiving emails
    • Streaming in High Definition (HD)

    NOTE: may not be suitable for high demand, low latency online gaming.

    Average busy period speed 7-11pm

    25 Mbps download
    5 Mbps upload

    Typical busy period speed range 7-11pm

    Download: 24 - 25 Mbps
    Upload: 4 - 5 Mbps

    We’re still calculating typical busy period speeds (7-11pm) (averages and ranges) on this plan. The speed information is an estimate only and is subject to change. Speeds experienced may be slower, can vary due to a number of factors and will change over time.

    ‘Typical busy period speed range’ is the range of speeds that 5G internet services experience ~90% of the time. 

    Speeds experienced may be slower over Wi-Fi and can also be impacted by other factors such as the distance and line of sight between the serving 5G mobile tower and the modem, the number of users online, where your modem is located and how far you are from it, weather, congestions and your in-home set up.

    Essential 5G Internet speed

    Great for 1-3 people with heavy data use; or 3-5 people with light to moderate data use.

    • Making video calls, working
    • Streaming your favourite shows in HD
    • Emails, social media, browsing

    NOTE: may not be suitable for high demand, low latency online gaming.

    Your connection technology type

    Fibre To The Premises (FTTP)

    FTTP technology runs an optic fibre line from the nearest available fibre node directly to your premises.

    Your connection technology type

    Fibre To The Building (FTTB)

    FTTB technology runs an optic fibre line from the nearest available fibre node to your building’s communications room. From here, a copper line runs to your wall socket.

    Your connection technology type

    Fibre To The Node (FTTN)

    FTTN technology runs an optic fibre line from the nearest available fibre node in your street, or a nearby street with a final stretch of copper to your wall socket inside your premises.

    Your connection technology type

    Fixed Wireless (FW)

    FW technology starts at a Wireless tower. The tower sends the signal to a fixed antenna on your roof, which continues through internal wiring to your wall socket.

    Your connection technology type

    Hybrid Fibre Coaxial (HFC)

    HFC technology runs an optical fibre line from the nearest available fibre node to your street. From here, a coaxial cable runs to your wall socket.

    Your connection technology type

    Fibre To The Curb (FTTC)

    Optical Fibre leading to a small node in the telecommunications pit or mounted to the pole outside your premises. From the node, a copper telephone cable delivers the service to the wall socket inside your premises.
